text:
Alice M.: heads up — staging streaming p95 jumped a lot after the midnight deploy, looks correlated with tool-enabled flows. p95 ~420ms now vs ~110ms before :frowning:
Ben K.: which API path? streaming binary? or SSE? :thinking_face:
Alice M.: SSE /v1/generate/stream. non-tool-chat streams unchanged. only when tool_call metadata present in proto.
Carla R.: can you paste a sample trace/span waterfall? I want to see serialize vs flush timing.
Alice M.: https://grafana.redwood/staging/streams?panel=latency — span shows long wait in sse_writer.flush between token frames
deploy-bot: Deployment rld-20260312-7 started by Lucy at 2026-03-12T03:10Z — commits: 7 — PRs: #4321, #4319
Jordan: did CI perf pick this up? I remember a perf test hanging on small-token bursts last night.
Mike L.: CI perf noticed regression in serializer microbench after merge of PR #4321. p95 serialization cost up ~3x. see job 4321 logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/4321/perf
Carla R.: possible suspects: new frame aggregation, maybe kernel selection toggles in stream path. If aggregation waits, short-token streams will get buffered.
Ben K.: starting live pprof capture on staging run — grabbing cpu/flame graphs now.
Ben K.: flame excerpt from busy period:
```
  sse_writer.flush         35%  (sleep_and_write)
  serializer.emit_frame   30%  (append_tool_meta)
  kernel_select           10%  (choose_vector_impl)
  kv_cache.lookup         5%   (cache_hit)
```
Lucy: I changed frame bundling in PR #4321 — added an aggregation delay option (default 50ms) to reduce tiny writes. I thought it'd only affect high-throughput non-interactive flows.
Alice M.: repro script below simulates tool-enabled small tokens every 10ms. numbers show the delta:
```
# simulate short-streams with tool metadata
python tools/sim_stream.py --tokens 6 --interval 0.01 --tool true
# with aggregation 50ms -> p95 420ms
# with aggregation 0ms -> p95 110ms
```
Mike L.: git bisect between v1.7.2 (good) and v1.8.0 (bad) — first bad commit: 9f4de2b "stream: add frame aggregation delay" (author: Lucy)
Jordan: confirmed: toggling FRAME_AGG_DELAY=0 in env on staging immediately brings p95 back down. Looks like aggregation is the root cause, not kernel selection.
Carla R.: but why serialization microbench regressed in CI? maybe adding metadata serialization code path when tools present increased work per token. two orthogonal changes combined -> worse observed latency.
Ben K.: grep in PR shows new code path appends tool proto into every frame and runs base64 encoding for tool sigs before flush. that adds cpu per-frame and with delay causes larger coalesced frames and longer pause before first byte.
Lucy: hmm. my intent was to amortize syscalls; but for low-latency interactive streams this is harmful.
Alice M.: mitigation options:
- short-term: set FRAME_AGG_DELAY=0 for streaming routes when tool_call is enabled (hotfix)
- mid-term: make tool metadata serialization happen inline but async for non-essential fields, or piggyback on first write without blocking
- long-term: avoid base64 per-token; switch to chunked encoding or precompute signatures at model step
Mike L.: I can push a canary config to staging with FRAME_AGG_DELAY=0 for tool routes now. will monitor.
Jordan: logging note — add a metric for "sse_first_byte_latency" so we can separate serialization wait vs network write cost.
Ben K.: opened perf bug with samples and flame: PERF-2026-114
Lucy: I'll revert the default in a follow-up PR and add a feature flag gated by route type. Sorry for the regression — missed interactive case in my tests.
deploy-bot: Hotfix deployment started by Mike L. — rollback of rld-20260312-7 to rld-20260311-4
Alice M.: rechecked after hotfix: p95 back to ~115ms. thanks team :tada:
Carla R.: still want CI perf adjusted to include microburst streaming test (short tokens + tool metadata) to catch this class earlier.
Mike L.: noted — adding test to perf suite. link to draft test: https://git.redwood/tests/streaming/microburst
Lucy: will include careful perf notes in next PR. lesson learned.
Jordan: closing bisect, marking revert/rollout blocker in tracking board.
Alice M.: awesome, closing thread unless we see more regressions. thanks all.
